predecessors.name: Indus Valley Civilisation
predecessors.text: 'It is a successor of the Cemetery H culture and black and red ware culture (BRW) within this region' (Haryana, the Ghaggar-Hakra country)

predecessors.name: Ochre Coloured Pottery culture
predecessors.text: the Ochre Coloured Pottery page says 'The OCP was succeeded by this culture' (Ganga-Yamuna country); no more precise land is given

successors.name: Kuru
successors.text: the Kuru country: Hastinapur and Bhagwanpura (Kurukshetra) are PGW sites, and the page says the culture 'probably corresponds to the middle and late Vedic period, i.e., the Kuru-Panchala kingdom'

successors.name: Panchala
successors.text: Ahichchhatra, a major PGW site in Rohilkhand, the northern Panchala

successors.name: Surasena
successors.text: Mathura, a PGW site of 'around 375 hectares'

successors.name: Vatsa
successors.text: Kosambi, a PGW site at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence

ledger.x: c. 1200 BCE: the Painted Grey Ware culture appears in the Ghaggar valley and the upper Ganga region. Infobox 'c. 1200-600 BCE'; 'conventionally dated c.1200 to 600-500 BCE, or from 1300 to 500-300 BCE'; Uesugi's Period I (c. 1300-1000) 'when it makes its appearance in the Ghaggar valley and the upper Ganga region'.…

c. 1000 BCE: the culture spreads east into the western Ganga valley. Uesugi's Period II 'c. 1000-600 BCE: when it spreads into the western part of the Ganga valley'; 'Towards the end of the period, many of the PGW settlements grew into the large towns and cities'.

c. 600 BCE: the Painted Grey Ware period gives way to the Mahajanapadas. Infobox 'c. 1200-600 BCE', 'Followed by: Mahajanapadas'; the page also has 'It is succeeded by Northern Black Polished Ware c. 700-500 BCE' and Uesugi's Period III runs to 300 BCE, so the end is the Mahajanapada convention year, not a hard break.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from sites ('1,576 PGW sites'), not from frontiers: every edge is an interpolation between named sites.
